out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Modification to Section 4-205.10 Equipment Certification
violations.observation: The following items are intended for household use only and are not approved for use in a commercial food establishment: 1 DR UPR ref. Vissani
violations.corrective_action: Food equipment that is certified or classified for sanitation by an American National Standards Institute (ANSI) accredited certification program will be deemed to comply with Parts 4-1 and 4-2 of this chapter. Food equipment in a food establishment shall be certified of classified by an ANSI-accredited certification program, an equivalent certification program, or approved by the Regulatory Authority before installation and/or use. Advised the manager to label refrigeration unit (1 DR UPR ref Vissani) that is intended to use for employees-“Employee use only”. Advise the manager to replace the refrigeration unit with NSF within 90 days. The refrigeration unit was labeled”Employee Use Only” during inspection.

violations.title: Food Storage Container, Common Name
violations.observation: The following food items that are not easily identified by appearance were observed without a label: squeeze bottles of ketchup, mayonnaise, mustard.and etc.
violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. PIC labeled all squeeze bottles of aforementioned food items.

violations.title: Food Protection Manager - Accredited Program
violations.observation: It shall be unlawful to operate a food establishment unless it is under the immediate control of a certified food manager who has shown proficiency through passing an accredited examination. PIC was not able to provide a certified food manager certificate.
violations.corrective_action: Please obtain a certified food managers certificate from an accredited program.

violations.title: Cooling from 135F to 70F, No More than 2 Hours
violations.observation: The following cooked time/temperature control for safety food(s) are not being adequately cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours. Observed pastelitos (cooked chicken) sitting outside of refrigeration on the prep table at 84F more than 2 hours.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety foods shall be cooled from 135F to 70F within two hours to prevent the growth of harmful bacteria. Foods that have been temperature abused are to be discarded. EHS discussed proper cooling procedures with PIC. PIC discarded pastelitos.

out_items.name: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control

violations.title: Methods to Facilitate Proper Cooling
violations.observation: The following methods used for cooling were not adequate to facilitate proper cooling: Pastelitos (cooked chicken) found at 84F at the time of inspection, were observed sitting outside of refrigeration for more than 2 hr.
violations.corrective_action: Cooling hot foods shall be accomplished as follows: 1) placing the food in shallow pans; 2) separating the food into smaller or thinner portions; 3) using rapid cooling equipment; 4) stirring the food in a container placed in an ice water bath; 5) using containers that facilitate heat transfer; 6) adding ice as an ingredient; or other effective methods. Food containers placed in cooling and cold equipment to cool shall be: 1) arranged in the equipment to provide maximum heat transfer through the containers walls, and 2) loosely covered or uncovered as long as protected from contamination to facilitate heat transfer from the surface of the food. EHS discussed proper cooling methods with PIC. Pastelitos must be cooled to 70F within 2 hours as part of the proper cooling procedure.
